subsystems.name: HTTP Adapter Helpers
subsystems.description: This subsystem provides the low-level networking utilities that adapters lean on: proxy tunneling, HTTP/2 session reuse, streaming transform helpers, multipart form-data generation, URL/data-URI parsing and environment detection. It is separated from the core request engine so that transport-specific concerns stay swappable and are shared by the HTTP, XHR and fetch adapters without entangling them with config resolution. Data flow starts when an adapter serializes a body with lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js:68 and pipes it through lib/helpers/AxiosTransformStream.js:8 for backpressure, while lib/adapters/http.js:258's setProxy and lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:274 decide whether traffic must tunnel. The HTTP adapter then reuses connections through lib/helpers/Http2Sessions.js:11 and decompresses responses with lib/helpers/ZlibHeaderTransformStream.js:5. These helpers connect outward to lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js and the request dispatch path, and are consumed by neighbouring adapters such as lib/adapters/xhr.js, which rely on the same environment flags from lib/platform/common/utils.js:35.

files.role: Implements the Node.js HTTP/HTTPS adapter, using the helper functions in this subsystem to manage proxies, redirects, decompression and HTTP/2 transport. It is the largest consumer of the proxy and stream helpers, and it is where a request handed off by dispatchRequest is transformed into Node socket activity.

subsystems.name: Core Request Engine
subsystems.description: The core request engine owns the client-side lifecycle: it creates a configured Axios object, merges user/default/instance config, normalizes headers, runs interceptor chains and applies request/response transforms. It exists as its own subsystem because every adapter must receive exactly the same resolved configuration and because request orchestration is independent of the transport that eventually executes it. A call flows through the Axios class (lib/core/Axios.js:22), which uses mergeConfig (lib/core/mergeConfig.js:28) and resolveConfig (lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js:25) to produce the final settings, then applies header normalization via AxiosHeaders (lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:198) and user hooks registered on InterceptorManager (lib/core/InterceptorManager.js:34). transformData (lib/core/transformData.js:15) and utilities in lib/utils.js:461 shape payloads before control passes to the adapter layer. This subsystem connects to lib/defaults/index.js for defaults, to lib/adapters/adapters.js for transport selection, and to lib/helpers/buildURL.js:31 and lib/helpers/sanitizeHeaderValue.js:46 to prepare the concrete request.

subsystems.name: Public API Dispatch
subsystems.description: The public API dispatch layer is the user-facing surface of the library: it builds the default axios singleton, creates custom instances, selects which adapter will run, performs pre-dispatch cancellation checks and exposes shared symbols for cancel and error handling. It is separate so that the externally visible contract (create, all, spread, isAxiosError, CancelToken) is not buried in the request engine and so adapter selection is centralized. createInstance (lib/axios.js:28) constructs an Axios instance and attaches helpers at lib/axios.js:66 and lib/axios.js:80, while getAdapter (lib/adapters/adapters.js:65) maps configured adapter names to concrete implementations. When a request is issued, dispatchRequest (lib/core/dispatchRequest.js:34) first calls throwIfCancellationRequested (lib/core/dispatchRequest.js:17) and then hands off to the chosen adapter. Cancellation is coordinated by CancelToken (lib/cancel/CancelToken.js:12), whose then/abort/unsubscribe methods drive lib/cancel/CanceledError.js:5, and user code can recognize those failures with isCancel (lib/cancel/isCancel.js:3). Neighbouring subsystems include lib/core/Axios.js for the instance internals, lib/adapters/adapters.js for dispatch, and lib/core/AxiosError.js which is the error type surfaced by dispatchRequest.

subsystems.name: XHR Adapter Utilities
subsystems.description: This subsystem contains the browser XHR transport and the URL/progress utilities that support it. It is isolated from the Node HTTP stack because the XHR event model, cancellation and progress semantics are browser-specific and should not affect the shared request engine. The adapter decides availability with isXHRAdapterSupported (lib/adapters/xhr.js:14) and handles terminal states via done (lib/adapters/xhr.js:27), onloadend (lib/adapters/xhr.js:43) and onreadystatechange (lib/adapters/xhr.js:108), while onCanceled (lib/adapters/xhr.js:217) bridges cancellation from CancelToken. URL building uses buildFullPath (lib/core/buildFullPath.js:68), combineURLs (lib/helpers/combineURLs.js:11) and isAbsoluteURL (lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js:10), and protocol validity is checked by normalizeURLForProtocolCheck (lib/helpers/normalizeURLForProtocolCheck.js:12). Progress reporting is throttled with progressEventReducer (lib/helpers/progressEventReducer.js:5), speedometer (lib/helpers/speedometer.js:9) and throttle (lib/helpers/throttle.js:7), and settle (lib/core/settle.js:14) finalizes the promise. The subsystem connects to lib/adapters/adapters.js for registration, lib/core/Axios.js for request invocation, and lib/cancel/CanceledError.js for aborted requests.

subsystems.name: Fetch Adapter Validation
subsystems.description: This subsystem implements the Fetch adapter for browsers and the validation, signal-composition, and body-length-estimation utilities that support it. It exists as a separate unit because the Fetch adapter has different request, cancellation, and body-size constraints than the XHR or Node http adapters, so those concerns are isolated rather than mixed into the core dispatch path. The `factory` function in lib/adapters/fetch.js:68 builds the adapter, using `resolveBodyLength` and `getBodyLength` to size the payload, `trackRequestStream` and `onChunkProgress` for progress events, and `maybeWithAuthCredentials` plus `decodeURIComponentSafe` for request preparation. `composeSignals` merges user and internal abort signals, while `estimateDataURLDecodedBytes` estimates decoded data-URL body sizes and `validator`'s `assertOptions` validates configuration. It connects to the rest of the library through lib/adapters/adapters.js, lib/axios.js, lib/core/Axios.js, and lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js, and its behavior is covered by tests/unit/adapters/fetch.test.js and the listed helper tests.

subsystems.description: This subsystem is the ESLint flat configuration for the whole repository. It exists as a separate unit so code-style and correctness rules are declared once at the root instead of being scattered through source files or package scripts. ESLint loads eslint.config.js when linting lib/, tests/, and build scripts, and every file in the repository is checked against it; because it is configuration rather than runtime code, there is no data flow through it. Its only observable effect is constraining the code that all other subsystems produce, and it has no runtime dependencies, which is why its related_files list is empty.

files.role: Flat ESLint configuration for the repository, defining parser, plugins, rules, and ignores for all source and test files.

subsystems.name: TypeScript Definitions
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the complete TypeScript type-definition surface for the axios library, declaring the public contracts for requests, responses, headers, errors, cancellation, interceptors, and the axios factory. It exists as a separate unit because the JavaScript runtime implementation cannot express compile-time types; separating the declarations lets consumers get IDE autocompletion and type checking without coupling the type system to the executable code. Data flows through these declarations as static shapes only: an application builds an AxiosRequestConfig (index.d.ts:391), the library returns an AxiosResponse (index.d.ts:515) or throws an AxiosError (index.d.ts:524), and users obtain instances via the AxiosStatic factory (index.d.ts:766). The Axios class (index.d.ts:646) and AxiosInstance (index.d.ts:710) define how requests are invoked, while AxiosHeaders (index.d.ts:25) and CancelToken (index.d.ts:599) describe helpers used during request lifecycle. The related_files list for this subsystem is empty, so the file is not shown importing or being imported by other scanned subsystems; instead it is consumed externally by TypeScript projects that install the package.

files.role: Central type declaration file for the axios public API. It defines every exported interface, class, type alias, and factory signature that TypeScript consumers rely on, and it mirrors the runtime API without containing implementation logic.

subsystems.name: FormData Environment Class
subsystems.description: This subsystem isolates the environment-specific FormData implementation so the rest of the library can use a single import point. It exists as a separate unit because FormData is supplied by the host runtime and must not be assumed or directly instantiated by request code. The module lives at lib/env/classes/FormData.js and is consumed by environment-abstraction code whenever multipart data is prepared. Rather than exposing a single named function, it provides a class-style module that guards or resolves the runtime FormData. It connects to neighbouring subsystems through ordinary imports from the environment layer; no related files were listed, so it is best understood as a leaf dependency used during request serialization.

files.role: Provides the runtime FormData abstraction used by the environment layer. It fits the subsystem by giving multipart/request code a single import point that can resolve or guard the host FormData implementation.

subsystems.name: Deprecation Helper
subsystems.description: This subsystem provides the deprecatedMethod helper that logs consistent warnings when legacy APIs are invoked. It exists as a separate utility because deprecation messaging is needed from multiple methods, and duplicating the warning logic would produce inconsistent output. The helper is declared at lib/helpers/deprecatedMethod.js:15 and is called with the deprecated method's name and any replacement or documentation details. When a deprecated method runs, it invokes deprecatedMethod, which formats the message and writes it to the console. It has no listed related files, so its connections are through helper imports from core modules that still expose old API names.

files.role: Defines the deprecatedMethod warning helper used by legacy API wrappers. It fits the subsystem by centralizing deprecation message formatting so all old APIs warn consistently.

key_symbols.name: deprecatedMethod
key_symbols.explanation: Formats and logs a deprecation warning when a legacy method is called. It runs synchronously at the start of the wrapper that still exposes the old API.

subsystems.name: Null Helper
subsystems.description: This subsystem is a minimal library helper for null-related checks or values, implemented in lib/helpers/null.js. It exists as a separate unit to keep a trivial but frequently reused null operation in one place and to avoid scattering null logic across the request pipeline. As a helper module, it is imported by other lib/helpers and core modules that need to detect or represent null values. Data flows through its exported function: arguments are evaluated and a null result or flag is returned to the caller. No related files were recorded, so its connections are through the normal helper-import mechanism rather than a dedicated subsystem boundary.

files.role: Provides a shared null-related utility for the helper layer. It fits the subsystem by giving modules a single import for null checks or null-value handling.

subsystems.name: Rollup Configuration
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the Rollup build configuration that controls how the library is bundled into distributable artifacts. It exists as a separate module so build inputs, output filenames, globals, plugins, and externalization rules stay out of the runtime source. At config load time, require (rollup.config.js:11) and lib (rollup.config.js:12) set up module loading and library metadata, while outputFileName (rollup.config.js:13), name (rollup.config.js:14), namedInput (rollup.config.js:15), and defaultInput (rollup.config.js:16) define bundle naming and entries. buildConfig (rollup.config.js:18) creates each target's Rollup options, and build (rollup.config.js:25) applies those options for every configured output. nodeCjsExternal (rollup.config.js:67) decides which imports should remain external in CommonJS builds. The config's related_files list is empty, so its repository connections are indirect: it tells Rollup to compile the library entry files in lib/, which in turn pull in the rest of the helpers and core modules.

files.role: Central Rollup configuration for producing distributable bundles. It fits the subsystem by deriving bundle metadata and returning target-specific Rollup configs.

subsystems.name: Sandbox Server
subsystems.description: This subsystem is a small Node.js HTTP server used by the sandbox environment to serve static demo files and mock API responses. It exists as a separate unit to keep development tooling out of the library source and give contributors a runnable playground. The server reads PORT (sandbox/server.js:111) and passes every incoming request to requestHandler (sandbox/server.js:75). requestHandler routes it to handleApiRequest (sandbox/server.js:33) for API calls and to pipeFileToResponse (sandbox/server.js:14) for serving files. The API handler processes the request and writes a response, while the file helper streams static assets from disk. Although the scan lists no related files, the server is used during development to load the built library in a browser and exercise its behaviour.

files.role: Self-contained HTTP server for the sandbox and demo environment. It fits the subsystem by serving static fixtures and API responses so contributors can test the built library in a browser.

subsystems.name: Vitest Configuration
subsystems.description: This subsystem configures the Vitest test runner for the repository, telling Vitest how to discover and execute unit tests. It exists as a separate unit so that test execution settings are isolated from production build configuration and from runtime source code, making it easy to change test environments or coverage rules without touching application logic. Control flow starts when a developer invokes Vitest; the runner reads vitest.config.js at startup, applies the configured environment, transforms, and test globals, and then loads the test suite files. Because the related_files list is empty, this file is not shown importing or being imported by any other scanned subsystem; it acts as a standalone entry point consumed only by the Vitest CLI.

files.role: Configuration file for Vitest that defines how tests are matched, transformed, and executed. It is read directly by Vitest at startup and supplies the options that shape the test run.

subsystems.name: Webpack Configuration
subsystems.description: This subsystem provides the Webpack build configuration for the axios package, producing distributable bundles from the source tree. It exists as a separate unit because bundling concerns such as entry points, output formats, minification, and environment-specific targets differ sharply from runtime behavior and test setup, so isolating them keeps the build reproducible and maintainable. Control flows through the exported generateConfig function at webpack.config.js:3: Webpack invokes this function at configuration load time, and the returned config object drives module resolution, loaders, plugins, and output generation. The related_files list for this subsystem is empty, so the config is not shown importing or being imported by other scanned subsystems; instead it consumes source modules implicitly through the entry points it defines.

files.role: Webpack configuration module that generates build options for bundling the library. Its exported generateConfig function is called by Webpack during startup to produce the final configuration used for compilation.

key_symbols.name: generateConfig

overview.description: This repository implements the axios HTTP client: the public API dispatch layer builds axios instances, selects transports, and handles cancellation, while the core request engine merges configuration, normalizes headers, and runs interceptors before handing requests to an adapter. Transport-specific implementations (HTTP, XHR, and Fetch) rely on shared adapter helpers, browser platform classes, and the FormData environment class for networking, serialization, and runtime-specific behavior, while the defaults and platform subsystem supplies environment-specific config and error/serialization utilities. Supporting utilities such as the deprecation and null helpers are used by core modules, and TypeScript definitions expose the runtime contracts to consumers. Build and development concerns—Rollup, Webpack, Vitest, linting, the sandbox server, and sandbox bootstrap—surround the library source and are kept separate from runtime code.
